text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
Business:
ADEVARUL
- The government discussed a package of bills, including the 1997 budget, the paper says.
- Five workers at the Calafat thermal power plant were killed when an old crane at the plant collapsed.
- Italian businessmen top list of foreign investors in Romania.
ROMANIA LIBERA
- Bakeries will get 300,000 tonnes of wheat coming from the state reserves.
- The Brasov-based Roman SA truck factory will ask its workers to take a one-week forced leave starting March 12.
- Private farmers will get credits worth 550 billion lei for seasonal farm works.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI
- Some 1.0 million pigs in state-run farms across the country are starving due to shortage of funds to buy fodder.
General:
ROMANIA LIBERA

- Closer ties between Romania and Hungary will increase the chances of the two countries to get NATO and European Union memership, Hungarian Prime Minister Gyla Horn said ahead of the visit of Prime Minister Victor Ciorbea to Budapest.

- Romania's integration in NATO will cost too much, the newspaper's editorial says. Romania can neither afford a defence budget amounting to three percent of the GDP nor "painful" basic treaties with neighbouring Ukraine and Moldova, which both hold former Romanian territories.
- Newspaper publishes excerpts of international treaties linked to the legal status of the Serpent Island in the Black Sea -- a sensitive issue in the draft of the basic treaty with Ukraine.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI
- Romanians smuggle sheep across the Danube to Serbia, on the route the used before to smuggle fuel in violation of United Nations sanctions imposed on former Yugoslavia.
- Health unions asked for a 4.5 percent of the GDP to be allocated for the health budget this year.
- President Emil Constantinescu praised the Romanian people for the way it accepts the painful costs of reforms.
- The Senate's health commission drafted a bill to ban human cloning, in reaction to wide international debates.
CURIERUL NATIONAL
- Bulgarians come by the hundreds to Bucharest market places to sell their products in exchange for food.
ADEVARUL
- Simion Simon, deputy rector of the Cluj-based Romanian-Hungarian University Babes-Bolyai slammed Ciorbea's plans to allow the creation of a separate Hungarian-language university.
-- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
